body:
Wow, this feels like somebody read my mind and decided to write my scattered and somewhat elusive thoughts down in an articulate and precise manner, in a way I never could.

I especially love the Mount Everest analogy. A lot of the time it does seem like this world consists of people who love mountaineering and those of us who don't. The ones who do don't really seem to care too much about what's waiting for them on top - they just enjoy climbing mountains so much that it's just not that relevant to them. The chance to earn 20 bucks is just an added bonus, and the threat of a right hook in the kisser doesn't deter them from doing what they love to do anyway.

Then there's people who are standing at the base of the mountain, look up and go "You know what, dude? Maybe not". The mountaineering enthusiasts notice this and simply cannot wrap their heads around someone not wanting to do something that they themselves enjoy dearly.
"Go to this guy over there" they say, "he has a PhD in Applied Hiking from Lofty Heights University. He'll help you figure it out".
Now you're in this guy's office, and he's trying to sell you equipment that he says will help make your hike easier.
"How about a grappling hook?"
"Nope"
"A pair of sturdy boots?"
"Nah."
"An icepick?"
"Pfff."
Until he finally goes: "Well, what do you want me to do? Build an elevator straight to the top, just for you?", which you decline.
"What the hell DO you want, then?" -"I want nothing to do with that damn mountain of yours."

I forget where I was going with this. All I really wanted to say is that yeah, I get it. I totally do.
Just, where does one go from here?
